flawed_step: Line 52: checking only M_(2,3) does not justify claiming that S_2 generates automorphisms of H_1 ∪ H_2 ∪ H_3, because edges between H_1 and H_3 are ignored.
counterexample: Let G=H with blocks H1={a0,a1}, H2={b0,b1}, H3={c0,c1}, each having no internal edges. Put matching edges a0-b0,a1-b1 between H1,H2; matching edges b0-c0,b1-c1 between H2,H3; and only the edge a0-c0 between H1,H3. Let each beta_i contain the identity and the swap of its block, so all hypotheses hold (the global identity is an isomorphism). The first iteration accepts the simultaneous swap of H1 and H2, so it belongs to <S1>. In the second iteration, combining it with the swap of H3 gives q=(a0 a1)(b0 b1)(c0 c1). This preserves M_(2,3), since it swaps both ends of the H2-H3 matching, and hence the line-52 procedure accepts it. But q sends the edge a0-c0 to a1-c1, which is not an edge. Thus q is not an automorphism of H1∪H2∪H3.
assessment_summary: The iterative construction loses constraints between nonconsecutive blocks. The explicit accepted permutation above is not an automorphism of the accumulated graph, invalidating the claimed construction and therefore the proof.
